protocol.connection_model: closed-loop persistent KV connections, one in-flight SET per client
protocol.primary_metric: SET fully sent at or before WAL data fsync entry and still unacknowledged at or after fsync exit

method.trace: strace timestamps fsync entry; -T duration gives exit
method.clock: CLOCK_REALTIME nanoseconds for client and strace correlation
method.primary_pending_count: count(SET send_completed_ns <= fsync_start_ns and SET acknowledged_ns >= fsync_end_ns)

supplementary_counts.pending_at_start_count: fully sent before fsync entry and unacknowledged after entry
supplementary_counts.pending_at_end_count: fully sent before fsync exit and unacknowledged after exit
supplementary_counts.arrivals_during_count: fully sent during fsync and unacknowledged after exit
supplementary_counts.overlap_count: fully sent before fsync exit and unacknowledged at/after entry

method.window_filter: successful fsync to a wal-NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN.log file with entry timestamp inside the measured client window
method.counter_invariant: measured-window STATS deltas must equal successes and parsed WAL data fsync windows

checks.name: counter_and_trace_invariants
checks.requirement: successes == WAL appends == WAL data fsyncs == SYNC mutations == trace windows; no failed or unresolved WAL fsyncs

limitations: WSL2 loopback, single node, same-host client and server; not a production SLA or capacity claim.
Closed-loop clients with one outstanding SET each; this measures request-level opportunity, not open-loop saturation.
The pending count is an external upper-bound opportunity: it does not prove that a future server queue already contains those records or that a writer thread can batch them without overhead.
Client acknowledgement timestamps include client scheduling and Python wake-up delay; they can only overstate pending duration.
strace ptrace and tracing overhead affects timing and is present for every measured fsync window.
The experiment does not test correctness, crash recovery, queue bounds, completion ordering, or the G4 throughput gate.
Passing G3 only authorizes a separate implementation-level ADR; it does not authorize merging group commit into the write path.
